kind_note: Pollard rho on classes {P, -P} (representative: smaller ordinate), the 16-jump r-adding walk with BKL look-ahead against fruitless 2-cycles, Brent detection of longer fruitless cycles and a deterministic escape (double the cycle minimum). Validator: code read, and a Python port re-ran all 64 measured runs and reproduced every emitted field except ms.
protocol: research/blindspots_20261018/14-prime-m4-cells/PROTOCOL-ADDENDUM-rho-neg.md (addendum B to PROTOCOL.md, committed in 9b2f5e1b36 before the run): 'The matched reference for the gate is rho-neg (kind: negation). Plain rho is still reported beside it, priced at the same three weights.' Everything not changed by the addendum is PROTOCOL.md's matched rho: same make_jumps (16 jumps, four random bits per scalar, counted doubling chains), same partition, theta = max(bits/4, 2), DP rule x mod 2^theta = 0, cap 20*2^theta + 64, x-keyed table, counted verification mul(cand, G) == Q, 16 logarithms per cell, one thread, setup counted in gae.
unit: GAE: one counted affine group addition (doubling and P + (-P) included) = 1, plus w x native operations, w in {0, 0.1, 1}. Native set (same counters on every arm): lookup, insert, legendre, sqrt, rowop, madd, dptest, build, and for rho-neg canon, lookahead, cyctest (zero on every other arm). Recomputed natives: rho-neg = lookup + insert + dptest + canon + lookahead + cyctest; plain rho = lookup + insert + dptest; arm (a) = lookup + insert + legendre + sqrt + rowop. Cost(w) = mean over 16 runs of (gae + w * native), setup included.

evidence.matches_protocol: rho_neg_run/neg_step/canon/cmd_rho_neg read against the addendum's 'rho-neg algorithm (exact)': classes, look-ahead, Brent, escape, counting, row fields and seeds as specified; everything else is rho_run's code (make_jumps, start chain, theta, mask, cap, table, collision algebra, verification). The validator's port reproduced all 64 rho-neg rows and all 64 continuity rho rows field by field (except ms) from the addendum's target and seed formulas; 16/16 ok per cell.
evidence.strongest_available: every cell: p prime > 3, a, b != 0, j not in {0, 1728} => Aut(E) = {+-1}; E(F_p) has prime order n = #E(F_p) (G of order n, n prime in the Hasse interval and > 4 sqrt p), so no 2-torsion; the p-power Frobenius fixes E(F_p) pointwise and gives no class reduction. Negation (classes of size 2) is the largest usable automorphism group. Per-cell facts in validator-report-rhoneg.json.
evidence.same_unit: one instrument, one counter set: gae = counts.gadd for both rhos and total.gadd for arm (a); the new rho-neg counters are priced as native operations exactly like dptest (the addendum's pricing note; conservative against rho-neg at high w).
evidence.same_binary_or_process: see binary_or_process; continuity rows equal the recorded rows except ms at all four cells.

gae_band_cell.definition: ic = mean(gae_total) + w * mean(native_total) over 16 arm (a) full-IC runs (raw/fullic-a-b28.jsonl); rho = mean(gae) + w * mean(native) over 16 rho-neg runs (raw/rho-neg/rho-neg-b28.jsonl)

order_note: At every design cell and every w in {0, 0.1, 1}, rho-neg AND plain rho are both cheaper than arm (a) full IC (the addendum requires an order statement to hold against both). The two rhos change order inside the band: rho-neg is cheaper at ['16 bits w=0', '16 bits w=0.1', '20 bits w=0', '24 bits w=0', '28 bits w=0'], plain rho at ['16 bits w=1', '20 bits w=0.1', '20 bits w=1', '24 bits w=0.1', '24 bits w=1', '28 bits w=0.1', '28 bits w=1'] (rho-neg's canon, lookahead and cyctest are priced like dptest), so which rho is cheaper is unresolved at that boundary; the distance remaining for arm (a) is S / min(rho-neg, plain rho), reported per cell as gap_S_over_cheaper_rho.
